title: Site Reliability Engineer (m/w/d)
description:
einleitung
Zur Verstärkung unseres Product Gameserver Teams suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt eine:n Site Reliability Engineer (m/w/d ), der/die unseren Bereich aktiv mitgestaltet.
Als SRE (m/w/d) bist du Architekt:in und Verteidiger:in unserer Infrastruktur und sorgst für maximale Uptime, Performance und Stabilität – damit Millionen von Spieler:innen jederzeit ein reibungsloses Spielerlebnis genießen können.
deine aufgaben
Herrscher:in der Cluster: Du bist verantwortlich für den reibungslosen und hochverfügbaren Betrieb unserer Kubernetes-Cluster. Du skalierst, wartest und optimierst die Umgebung, in der unzählige Gaming-Abenteuer stattfinden.
Jäger:in der Latenz und Bugs: Du stellst den reibungslosen Betrieb unserer in Golang geschriebenen Kubernetes-Operatoren und anderer Services sicher. Performance-Optimierung und das Aufspüren von Fehlern sind für dich wie eine spannende Quest, um den Spieler:innen das bestmögliche Erlebnis zu garantieren.
Terraform-Architekt:in: Du entwirfst mit Terraform den Bauplan für unsere Infrastruktur. Du schaffst durch Infrastructure as Code (IaC) eine automatisierte und reproduzierbare Basis, auf der unsere Kundinnen und Kunden ihre eigenen digitalen Königreiche errichten können.
Ansible-Dompteur:in: Wiederkehrende manuelle Aufgaben sind deine Endgegner. Mit Ansible automatisiert du Konfigurationsmanagement, Deployments und alles andere, was dir im Weg steht, um eine stabile und konsistente Umgebung zu schaffen.
Wächter:in über die Performance: Du entwickelst und pflegst unsere Monitoring-, Logging- und Alerting-Systeme (z.B. mit Prometheus & Grafana), um Probleme zu erkennen, bevor sie zu einem "Game Over" führen.
dein profil
Kubernetes-Veteran: Du hast tiefgreifende, praxiserprobte Erfahrung im Betrieb, Management und Troubleshooting von Kubernetes-Clustern in einer Produktivumgebung.
Infrastructure as Code ist dein Credo: Du sprichst fließend Terraform und hast damit bereits komplexe Infrastrukturen aufgebaut und verwaltet.
Automatisierung im Blut: Du besitzt starke Kenntnisse in Ansible und nutzt es, um manuelle Prozesse zu eliminieren und die Effizienz zu steigern.
Ein Herz für Stabilität: Du denkst in Konzepten wie SLAs, SLOs und Error Budgets und hast eine Leidenschaft dafür, hochverfügbare und resiliente Systeme zu bauen.
Entwicklungserfahrung in Go : Du hast bereits Erfahrungen in der Entwicklung mit Go und liebst die Sprache für ihre Effizienz und Nebenläufigkeit. Du hast Kubernetes Operatoren in Go entwickelt und kannst bestehende in ihrer Laufzeit optimieren.
Gamer-Mindset: Du verstehst, was Spieler:innen von einer perfekten Plattform erwarten.
Kommunikationsstarker Teamplayer: Du schätzt den Austausch im Team, bringst dich aktiv ein und vermittelst komplexe technische Sachverhalte klar auf Englisch (Deutschkenntnisse sind ein Plus).
OnCall: Du nimmst an einer fair gestalteten Rufbereitschaft teil und übernimmst Verantwortung für die Zuverlässigkeit und Verfügbarkeit der Gameserver unserer Kunden.
Remote Setup : Du arbeitest remote innerhalb von +/- 2 Stunden zur Mitteleuropäischen Zeit (CET) und besitzt eine gültige EU-Arbeitserlaubnis (kein Relocation-Support). Über deine Teilnahme an unseren optionalen Teamtreffen (1x pro Quartal) freuen wir uns sehr!
deine benefits
Gaming im Herzen: Wir bieten kostenlose Nitrado Game Server für Gamer und eine einladende Community für alle, die sich wohlfühlen möchten, selbst wenn du kein/e Gamer:in bist. Entdecke, wie Nitrado mehr ist als nur Gaming - eine offene Community für Technologie und Kreativität.
Vertrauensarbeitszeit: Passe deine Arbeitszeiten an deine persönlichen Bedürfnisse an, um eine bessere Work-Life-Balance zu erreichen.
Remote Work: Unsere agilen Teams arbeiten Hand in Hand von ihrem bevorzugten Standort aus zusammen, sei es in unseren modernen Büros in Karlsruhe oder Berlin oder vollständig remote.

title: Security Engineer (m/w/d)
description:
Shopware ist ein führendes E-Commerce-System , das es Unternehmen weltweit ermöglicht, im digitalen Handel schnell und effizient zu skalieren. Als zukunftsweisende Open-Source-Lösung wird Shopware bereits von einigen der größten europäischen Marken, Einzelhändlern und Herstellern im B2C- und B2B-Bereich eingesetzt.
Hilf dabei, Shopware-Produkte sicherer zu machen, indem du während der gesamten Produktentwicklung Sicherheitsrisiken aufdeckst und reduzierst. Du arbeitest mit den Produktentwicklungsteams daran, Schwachstellen zu untersuchen, sichere Konzepte und Tests zu verbessern und praxisnahe Maßnahmen aufzubauen, die wiederkehrende Probleme in Commerce Core, Services und angrenzenden Produktbereichen verhindern.
Product Security Engineering ist eine Engineering-Funktion . Die Produktteams bleiben dafür verantwortlich, ihren eigenen Code zu korrigieren und zu testen. Dieses Team bringt gezielte Sicherheitsexpertise, eine gemeinsame Roadmap zur Prävention und eine klare Koordination für produktübergreifende Sicherheitsarbeit ein.
Requirements
Untersuche Schwachstellenmeldungen, Sicherheitswarnungen, interne Findings und Nacharbeiten zu Sicherheitsvorfällen . Bewerte die technischen Auswirkungen und unterstütze dabei, bestätigte Aufgaben an die zuständigen Product Owner weiterzuleiten.
Arbeite direkt mit Entwicklerinnen und Entwicklern an sicherem Design, Threat Models, Code Reviews, Ursachenanalysen, Fixes und Regressionstests für besonders risikoreiche Produktbereiche.
Entwickle und verbessere wiederverwendbare Sicherheitskontrollen , Leitfäden für Entwicklerinnen und Entwickler, Tests für Missbrauchsszenarien und praxisnahe Automatisierung zur Erkennung und Behebung von Schwachstellen.
Unterstütze dabei, für Product-Security-Findings klare Verantwortlichkeiten, Schweregrade, Reaktionsziele, betroffene Versionen und Nachweise zum Abschluss festzuhalten.
Arbeite mit den Engineering-Teams von Commerce Core und Services an Sicherheitsaufgaben über verschiedene Repositories, unterstützte Versionen, APIs, Integrationen und das Extension-Ökosystem hinweg .
Unterstütze koordinierte Sicherheits-Releases : Ermittle betroffene Bereiche, prüfe technische Behebungen und stimme dich mit Engineering, Product Operations, Quality, InfoSec und DevRel ab.
Überführe Erkenntnisse aus Sicherheitsvorfällen und Releases in konkrete Änderungen am Engineering, Tests oder Tools. Verfolge anschließend nach, ob diese Maßnahmen übernommen werden.
Kommuniziere bei zeitkritischen Aufgaben klar und dokumentiere Entscheidungen in den vereinbarten GitHub- und Confluence-Einträgen, damit Teams den Status nicht aus Slack-Verläufen rekonstruieren müssen.
Wirke an gemeinsamen Teampraktiken mit und vertrete bei Bedarf den anderen Produktbereich.
Das bringst du mit:
Fundierte Erfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung und Interesse an Produkt- oder Anwendungssicherheit.
Praktische Kenntnisse typischer Risiken in der Anwendungssicherheit , etwa Schwachstellen bei Authentifizierung und Autorisierung, Zugriffskontrolle, Datentrennung, API-Sicherheit, Umgang mit Zugangsdaten, Injection und Abhängigkeiten.
Die Fähigkeit, produktiven Code und Tests zu lesen und zu ändern , Risiken für Entwicklerinnen und Entwickler verständlich zu erklären und wartbare Fixes mit umzusetzen.
Erfahrung mit Threat Modeling, Sicherheitstests, Schwachstellenanalysen oder Secure Code Reviews ; in einigen Bereichen bringst du fundiertes Wissen mit, in anderen möchtest du dich weiterentwickeln.
Gutes Urteilsvermögen bei der Einschätzung von Schweregrad, Auswirkungen auf Kundinnen und Kunden und Ausnutzbarkeit sowie bei der Frage, wann ein Problem sofort eskaliert werden muss.
Klare schriftliche Kommunikation und die Fähigkeit, bei unklaren oder dringenden Aufgaben teamübergreifend zusammenzuarbeiten.
Kenntnisse von PHP sowie mit Shopwares Produkten, Services oder dem Extension-Ökosystem sind hilfreich.

title: Backend Engineer Internship
description:
Overview: Supply Chain API and Microservices Development
The Backend Engineer is a hands-on role responsible for the development, scaling, and maintenance of the core API services that power our entire integrated platform. You will build highly reliable, secure, and performant backend services within the NestJS modular monolith, focusing on critical supply chain logic, complex payment integrations, and the orchestration backbone for our AI agents.
Internship Details
Duration: 3 months
Start Date: Immediate
Location: Remote
Stipend: None initially. Based on your first-quarter performance, you may be offered a paid full-time opportunity, or even be absorbed directly by the client as an FTE.
Key Responsibilities & Core Projects
You will own the backend development for the most complex domain logic, ensuring scalability and transactional integrity.
API Development & Implementation: Design, develop, and deploy highly scalable APIs for all platform components using Node.js 22 and NestJS within the TypeScript modular monolith. This includes the backends for the e-commerce checkout, internal tool APIs, and the B2B portal.
SCM Domain Logic: Implement complex, transactional business logic within the core supply chain modules: Order Management (OMS), Warehouse Management (WMS), and Manufacturing Execution (MES). Ensure data integrity using PostgreSQL 15.
Integrations & Payments: Implement secure, reliable integrations with third-party payment gateways and external shipping/logistics providers.
Performance & Reliability: Implement effective caching strategies using Redis to boost API performance. Design and implement asynchronous processing and event-driven workflows to ensure system reliability and handle high-volume operations.
Security & Monitoring: Ensure all services adhere to security standards (JWT authorization, API security). Integrate backend services with the observability stack (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Loki) for monitoring and tracing.
Required Technologies & Tools
Candidates must possess deep, hands-on experience with our core backend and data stack:
Core Backend: Expert proficiency in Node.js 22, NestJS, and TypeScript (mandatory).
Data Layer: Strong expertise in PostgreSQL 15 (schema design, query optimization) and utilizing Redis for caching.
Architecture: Experience designing and implementing APIs (REST/GraphQL), asynchronous communication, and event-driven patterns.
Workflow: Experience working within a Monorepo structure, contributing to CI/CD via Makefile, and utilizing Docker for local development.
AI Agent Focus
You will build the reliable, secure services required for AI agent orchestration.
Agent Orchestration: Develop the backend services and API endpoints necessary to securely orchestrate, manage, and scale the AI agent systems.
Data Access Services: Implement secure, high-performance services that allow AI agents (using frameworks like LangChain) to access and write necessary data to the WMS/OMS modules without compromising transactional integrity.
Success Metrics & Career Path
Performance will be measured by:
Service Reliability: Uptime and stability of deployed services, achieving defined SLOs.
Code Quality & Efficiency: Delivery of clean, well-tested, and performant code that scales effectively.
Feature Velocity: Timely and efficient delivery of complex backend features, particularly within the critical OMS and WMS modules.
Mentorship Structure: Reports to the Technical Architect or Engineering Lead, working directly with Frontend, QA, and SRE teams to deliver high-quality supply chain functionality.

title: AI Research
description:
AI Researcher
About Vetto
Vetto builds the infrastructure for next-generation AI training data. We partner with the world’s top AI labs to push the frontier of what models can do — by designing, collecting, and delivering the highest-quality training data for the hardest problems in AI.
AI Researchers at Vetto figure out how to teach models new capabilities and how to tell whether it worked. You’ll design datasets and evaluations, run experiments, study model failures, and turn what you learn into better data and training strategies.
Most of our work is evaluation-driven, with some fine-tuning and post-training used to validate research hypotheses. You won’t be expected to build the infrastructure alone: you’ll work with an engineering team that builds the platforms and tools behind the research. You should still be comfortable writing code, analyzing data, and moving your own experiments forward.
Why Vetto ?
End-to-end ownership. You’ll take research questions from an initial idea to a dataset, benchmark, experiment, and useful conclusion.
Direct collaboration with top AI labs. Your work will help frontier teams understand their models and decide what data or training approach to try next.
Work that gets used. Your research can become training data, evaluations, technical reports, open benchmarks, and published papers.
A wide range of hard problems. Depending on the project, you might work on agents, model evaluations, human or synthetic data, failure analysis, or post-training.
Fast, flat team. You’ll ship experiments in days, not quarters.
What You’ll Do
Design and run experiments to understand model behavior, test new ideas, and determine whether a dataset or training intervention actually works.
Use fine-tuning and post-training experiments when useful to validate research hypotheses and measure improvements in the capabilities we care about.
Create datasets, benchmarks, agent environments, rubrics, and evaluation methods for problems that are not well measured today.
Work directly with AI labs and enterprise partners to turn open-ended model-development goals into concrete research and data projects.
Dig into model outputs and trajectories to understand systematic failure modes and separate model limitations from problems in the data, grader, or evaluation setup.
Write analysis code and build lightweight tools or prototypes for your own work, with support from engineers when a workflow needs to become reliable infrastructure.
Share what you learn through clear technical reports, internal discussions, benchmarks, and research papers.
What We’re Looking For
Must-haves:
Experience doing empirical research or similarly open-ended technical work with machine learning systems.
Hands-on experience designing and running agentic systems for complex work, such as coding agents and automated research pipelines.
Good experimental judgment: you can form a hypothesis, choose useful baselines and metrics, run a careful experiment, and make sense of noisy results.
Strong Python and data analysis skills, plus enough software engineering ability to prototype your own research workflows.
The independence to take an ambiguous question about a model and turn it into a dataset, benchmark, experiment, or other concrete contribution.
Rigorous analytical thinking — you look at the underlying evidence, notice subtle failure modes, and question results that seem too simple or too good to be true.
Excellent written and verbal communication with researchers, engineers, customers, and non-specialists.
Comfort with ambiguity, fast iteration, changing priorities, and occasional forward-deployed work with partner teams.
Nice to have:
Research or industry experience in LLM evaluation, post-training, agents, human or synthetic data, alignment, or AI safety.
Experience designing datasets or benchmarks, validating annotation quality, or working with large collections of model outputs and trajectories.

title: Developer Relations Engineer
description:
We’re Fly .io, and we’re building a new public cloud. We transmogrify containers into lightweight VMs and run them on our hardware around the world – hundreds of thousands of applications rely on us, running on every continent except Antarctica. If you haven’t already,take us for spin. Your app will be up and running in just minutes.
Unlike all the rest of our roles, these roles are geographically specific; devrel here is in large part about engaging local communities. We’re currently hiring devrel people who can deliver work full time in North America and Europe. Of course, our whole thing is that we deploy everywhere else in the world, too, so we’ll be expanding from there soon.
There are a lot DevRel jobs where you have to make your own fun, because the product is about eliminating some gnarly business slog like inventory management or expense tracking or underwriting. We’re not knocking those jobs! There’s nobility in eliminating slogs!
But this isn’t one of those jobs. We’re doing something big, something that’s about software development itself. We’re one of a number of upstart companies rethinking the public cloud, breaking down infrastructure problems that used to take months of work and dedicated headcount into a platform that our users can gain fluency with in a matter of minutes. If you’re our kind of developer, the fun in this job is built-in.
Folks working in DevRel at Fly .io interact with three different groups of people:
Group A: our product teams, like in every other devrel job: the people building the platform and its features.
Group B: our “framework” teams, which are a fun quirk of Fly .io: these are small teams of people organized around individual application frameworks like Rails, Django, Phoenix, and whatever people are doing in Javascript these days.
Group H: the “developer community”, a term the industry uses because it is apparently squicked out by the word “customer”.
You’ll accomplish this by deploying all of your “skills of an artist”, hopefully including things like:
Quickly building proof-of-concept applications that show off cool things about Fly .io, like how quickly you can start up a new VM, or the timeless elegance of our IPv6 addressing.
Building and delivering presentations for events, presentations that have the net effect of customers (err, the developer community) liking us more. Also, having the good taste to do this in ways that are interesting even to people who might never deploy an app on Fly .io.
Talking to people working on all kinds of applications, from side projects to large teams building microservice ensembles, and talking them through making the best use of Fly .io, the Fly Machines API, our integrations with products like Supabase, that sort of stuff.
Maintaining a public presence in online communities where developers congregate, and somehow doing all of this while maintaining your own authenticity and credibility. We’ll help!
25% monthly travel (with seasonal variability) to meet with developer communities in person to engage in small and large settings to build authentic developer interest in various regions and communities.
This Role Is A Good Fit For You If:
You enjoy building applications and are particularly psyched about the prototyping phase of building things, because there’s going to be a lot of that here.
The idea of a little bit of chaos appeals to you, because it’s a sign to you that there’s an opportunity to help define a new practice and make some big moves.
You’re opinionated enough to be interesting, but exceptionally good at listening, empathizing, and rolling with the opinions of our users. That’s a hard tradeoff and not a lot of us here can do it!
Your career goals involve increasing your public profile. We punch above our weight in getting attention from developers, and your job here would be part of building and expanding on that.

MixRank processes petabytes of data every month from web crawling. We have hundreds of customers using our data products including Google, Amazon, Facebook, Intel, and Adobe, across industries Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Security.

Overview: Supply Chain Security and Compliance
The Security Engineer is a critical role responsible for implementing and enforcing robust security practices across our entire integrated supply chain e-commerce platform. You will safeguard e-commerce transactions, secure internal tool integrations, and establish the trust framework for our AI agent operations, ensuring compliance with global regulatory standards like PCI-DSS and GDPR.
Internship Details
Duration: 3 months (extendable based on performance and project scope)
Start Date: Immediate
Location: Remote
Stipend: Unpaid initially; may convert to a paid internship, full-time role, or even direct client absorption (FTE) based on your performance
Key Responsibilities & Core Projects
You will secure all layers of the application, from the Next.js frontend to the NestJS modular monolith and the cloud infrastructure.
Security Architecture & Threat Modeling: Perform vulnerability assessments, code reviews, and threat modeling for all new features and systems, focusing on the critical MES $\rightarrow$ WMS $\rightarrow$ OMS business process flow.
Compliance Enforcement: Lead the implementation and auditing of security controls necessary for PCI-DSS compliance (for Payment module) and GDPR compliance (for user/tenant data handling).
Access Control & Authentication: Implement and manage secure API authentication methods, including OAuth 2.0 and SAML, utilizing Authentik/Ory Kratos and leveraging PostgreSQL's Row-Level Security (RLS) for tenant isolation.
Secrets & Encryption: Manage secrets and key rotation using Vault, define and enforce encryption protocols for data both in transit and at rest, and manage certificates via Traefik.
Abuse Prevention: Implement and monitor controls for API rate limiting, Web Application Firewall (WAF) rules, and traffic monitoring to prevent abuse and denial-of-service attacks.
Incident Response: Develop and practice incident investigation and response protocols. Conduct security awareness training for development and operations teams.
Required Technologies & Tools
Candidates must possess hands-on security experience with our core stack and compliance tools:
Platform Security: Node.js/NestJS security best practices, Next.js/React security, PostgreSQL RLS.
Compliance Focus: Experience with PCI-DSS and GDPR controls and auditing.
Authentication & Access: OAuth 2.0, SAML, JWT, Authentik/Ory Kratos.
Secrets & Infrastructure: HashiCorp Vault, Docker, Terraform.
Monitoring & Assessment: Tools for Static/Dynamic Application Security Testing (SAST/DAST).
AI Agent Security
You will be responsible for securing the emerging AI ecosystem.
Agent Trust Framework: Establish security boundaries for the AI agent interfaces, ensuring agents (built with LangChain/AutoGen) operate within strict permissions when accessing supply chain data (WMS, OMS).
Prompt Injection Prevention: Implement validation and sanitization techniques to mitigate prompt injection and data exfiltration risks in user-facing LLM interactions.
Success Metrics & Career Path
Performance will be measured by:
Security Scorecard: Reduction in identified vulnerabilities from assessments and code reviews (SAST/DAST).
Compliance Audits: Successful passing of regular PCI-DSS and GDPR audits.
Incident Handling: Speed and effectiveness of security incident investigation and remediation.
Mentorship Structure: Reports to the Solution Architect or Head of Technology, working closely with the development and DevOps teams to embed security into the CI/CD pipeline.

title: Senior Distributed Systems Engineer
description:
This is a remote position with in-person onboarding and retreats a few times a year.
About Vana
Vana is the leading decentralized AI network powered by user-owned data. Data is the most valuable resource in the digital world and it has been furthered by AI. Vana taps into the power of every individual to contribute data to leading AI models. Our guiding use case is a user-owned AI foundation model, collectively owned by 100 million users who've all contributed their data to it.
Projects like theReddit data DAO that onboarded 140k users are built on Vana. By building an open ecosystem to break down the walled gardens of tech giants, we are accelerating AI progress and giving users ownership in the AI models they create.
We got started out of MIT and have raised $20M from leading VCs including Paradigm and Polychain.
Role Overview
We’re looking for a Distributed Systems Engineer to help design and build the scalable infrastructure powering data access and compute in the Vana network.
You’ll be designing and building systems that allow users to connect their data in a privacy-preserving way, as well as pool and monetize it. As the backbone of Vana’s decentralized data layer, these systems move encrypted data across nodes, verify permissions through cryptographic proofs, and support ML workflows such as AI training and fine-tuning. They leverage Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) to ensure that no entity can ever access raw user data.
Here are some of the teams and projects that are already building on our infrastructure:
An EV startup collects video data of edge cases like near-collision events to train better driving models
A robotics-startup wants to fine-tune a model for grasping irregular objects
A fintech works on improving the correctness of their risk-modeling by analyzing transaction records in a GDPR-compliant way
Key Responsibilities
Lead the development of data query and compute layer with the goal of scaling it to process data required to train AI models applied to use-cases in EV, robotics, finances, healthcare and more
Design critical protocol mechanisms related to data privacy, permissioning and provenance applying recent cryptography techniques like ZK proofs, MCP, TEEs
Contribute to the development of Vana - EVM-compatible L1 blockchain specifically designed for user-owned data transactions
Develop comprehensive documentation and contribute to whitepapers, including collaborations with outside researchers and engineers from MIT and top AI labs/startups
Develop and implement robust debugging and troubleshooting processes for quick resolution of node-related issues in production environments
Participate in code reviews and provide technical guidance to team members
Minimum Qualifications
Experience in building large scale, secure, multi-node distributed systems
Experience designing pipelines for processing large amounts of data, ideally leveraging distributed data storage
Experience in Python, Go or similar languages in mission-critical systems
Experience profiling, debugging, and optimizing distributed systems for scale and performance
Some infrastructure experience with any of the top cloud platforms (GCP, AWS, Azure)
Experience in a fast-paced, async-first, globally distributed startup environment with rapid prototyping and iterative development.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in the compute-over-data space including sandboxed execution, data locality etc
Experience with ML workflows (cleaning data, training and fine-tuning models)
Experience with privacy preserving computation (TEEs, MPC, ZKP)
Experience or interest in decentralization technologies and web3 (protocol design, smart contracts development)
Track-record of significantly contributing to OSS

Who we are
MixRank processes petabytes of data every month from web crawling. We have hundreds of customers using our data products including Google, Amazon, Facebook, Intel, and Adobe, across industries Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Security.
Our team is 50+ full-time, full-remote from 20+ countries. We're growing, profitable, employee-owned, no dependence on outside funding. Applicants from all geographies and backgrounds are welcome.
We are looking for passionate individuals for whom programming is not just a job but it’s something they love to do. We're obsessed with computers, programming, big data, databases, compilers, hardware, math, data science, and the internet. Does this sound like you? Please apply to join our team.
Our code base is very friendly to new contributors. You'll have a fully-functional development environment within hours (fully automated) and be pushing commits on your first day. We operate at a larger scale than typical startups. We operate two datacenters with high performance servers we've built that are capable of dealing with the volumes of data we process. Unlike a typical startup where you'll spend half of your time in meetings, and the other half fixing bugs from Jira tickets— at MixRank you'll get to challenge yourself with difficult technical problems that will help you to grow as an individual.

We're hiring generalist software engineers to work on web applications, data mining, machine learning/data science, data transformation/ETL, data modeling, database scaling, infrastructure, devops, and more. We'll cater the role to whatever subset of these areas match your interests.
Beneficial (but optional!) experience includes PostgreSQL, Python, Rust, Linux, TypeScript, Nix, frontend/backend web development, and data mining.

title: Freelance Data Engineer (Postgres / Systemintegration)
description:
über juni
JUNI ist ein gemeinnütziges Ökosystem für Wissenschaft und Ausgründungen in Berlin. Wir betreiben unsere Programme über sieben SaaS-Tools hinweg — Newsletter, Events, Community, CRM, Formulare, Bewerbungen, Coworking — und darunter eine Postgres-Datenbank, die der eine Ort sein soll, an dem eine Person existiert.
Auf die Datenbank kommt es an. Ein aufgelöster Datensatz pro Person und pro Organisation, eine append-only-Zeile pro Interaktion, und ein deterministischer Weg zu entscheiden, zu welcher Person ein eingehender Payload gehört. Ziel ist, den Weg vom ersten Kontaktpunkt bis zum Meilenstein messbar zu machen. Die Verbindungsschicht zwischen den Tools und dieser Datenbank ist die Aufgabe.
deine aufgaben
Die Schicht bauen, die unsere Systeme mit einer Datenbank verbindet — in beide Richtungen — und uns dabei helfen, das Datenmodell richtig hinzubekommen.
Die Form der Daten steht weitgehend, und jedes neue System stellt sie auf die Probe. Quellen sind sich nicht einig, was als eine Person zählt, wann etwas passiert ist, und ob sie es zweimal melden. Das zu klären — und zu erkennen, wann das Modell angepasst werden muss, statt es um eine Quelle herumzubiegen — ist der Kern der Arbeit.
Wir suchen jemanden, der das mit uns durchdenkt und für einen bestimmten Entwurf argumentiert, nicht nur umsetzt, was spezifiziert ist.
dein profil
Umfang
Inbound Jedes System in die Datenbank. Mehrere Pipelines pro System — Quellen melden sehr unterschiedliche Dinge. Identitätsauflösung über Systeme hinweg. Outbound Manche Zustände entstehen bei uns, nicht im Tool. Die Datenbank entscheidet und schiebt an die Plattform, die es ausführt. Beide Richtungen sauber halten Plattformen melden zurück und widersprechen uns manchmal. Wer sich abgemeldet hat, darf nicht wieder hinzugefügt werden. Reporting KPI-Daten müssen in einem BI-Tool ankommen. Sie dorthin zu bringen gehört dazu, Dashboards bauen nicht. Suche Den Datenbestand in natürlicher Sprache durchsuchbar machen. Dokumentation Entscheidungen schriftlich, Pipelines in GitHub.
Nicht Teil der Rolle
Frontend. Es gibt keins und es ist keins geplant.
Voraussetzungen
Integration gegen Third-Party-APIs und Webhooks , in der Tiefe: Pagination, Retries, Signaturprüfung, Rate Limits, undokumentierte Payload-Strukturen, verspätete und vertauschte Events, Quellen, die bei jeder Änderung feuern und nicht sagen, was sich geändert hat.
Bidirektionale Synchronisation zwischen Systemen, die beide dasselbe Feld für ihres halten — Loop-Vermeidung, Echo-Unterdrückung, eine klare Antwort darauf, wer bei Konflikten gewinnt.
Postgres als Anwendungsdatenbank, nicht nur als Ziel. plpgsql-Funktionen, Trigger, Constraints und RLS, um Regeln beim Schreiben durchzusetzen. Wenn sich deine SQL-Erfahrung auf Transformationen nach dem Load beschränkt, passt die Rolle nicht.
Idempotenz als Gewohnheit, nicht als Nachgedanke. Eine Pipeline, die erneut läuft und nichts verändert, ist der Abnahmetest.
Sauberes Arbeiten mit Git — Migrationen, PRs, Review.
Arbeit mit personenbezogenen Daten unter der DSGVO, und ein Verständnis dafür, warum das einschränkt, was überhaupt eingelesen wird.
Englisch in Schrift. Die Arbeit läuft überwiegend asynchron, und was du baust, muss für jemanden lesbar sein, der nicht dabei war.
Hilfreich, nicht erforderlich
n8n oder ein anderer Orchestrator · Supabase · Relevanzarbeit an einem Suchindex — Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Meilisearch oder vergleichbar; Cluster-Betrieb ist nicht der Teil, den wir brauchen · Erfahrung als einzige Person auf einem System · Deutsch.
wir bieten
Zusammenarbeit
Remote und überwiegend asynchron, aber nicht wortlos — gerade am Anfang sind echte Gespräche eingeplant, während du dich in die Systeme und ihre Zusammenhänge einarbeitest.
Rahmen
Freiberuflich, Start so bald wie möglich. Zunächst drei Monate; danach sehen wir, was gebraucht wird.
Berlin oder Remote innerhalb der EU.

title: Senior Analytics Engineer
description:
About Imagine Worldwide
All children have immense potential, but hundreds of millions don’t have access to the learning they need. Imagine Worldwide believes that every child should be empowered with the basic right to literacy and numeracy. We provide an innovative education technology solution and implementation model to the global literacy/numeracy learning crisis using the onebillion application and various toolkits and systems to support implementation. Our model is massively scalable, evidence-based, and can deliver foundational learning to millions of the most marginalized children.
Imagine Worldwide partners with governments, organizations, and communities to provide child-directed, tablet-based learning that is accessible, effective, and affordable. We are incorporated in California (United States) as a nonprofit organization, but operate in Sub-Saharan Africa through locally-registered entities in Malawi, Sierra Leone, and Tanzania. Learn more on our website.
Role Overview
The Senior Analytics Engineer builds, runs and improves Imagine’s analytics platform: the infrastructure, pipelines and core data models that the organisation’s reporting and analysis depend on. The central task is to scale the platform as data volumes grow, keeping costs under control without giving up performance. In a small team, that means covering the infrastructure underneath the data as well as the data engineering itself.
Imagine’s data comes from many sources. The largest is tablets in more than 1,500 schools across Malawi, Tanzania and Sierra Leone, which record learning activity as individual events, adding up to billions of records. These only become meaningful when joined with programme context, such as active schools per term, device allocations and enrolment, and with operational data from inventory and field data collection. Turning all of this into reliable data on a non-profit budget calls for careful decisions about where processing happens and what each workload costs.
The role reports to the Director of Analytics, who sets the platform’s architecture and technical standards, and works alongside the rest of the Analytics Team. We are looking for someone senior who takes initiative, turns architectural direction into working systems, and brings forward evidence-based proposals for improving them. As the engineer builds context, they take on increasing ownership of the platform’s day-to-day running and technical decisions.
Key Responsibilities
The Senior Analytics Engineer’s responsibilities fall into four pillars. The first two cover the platform itself: the infrastructure it runs on, and the pipelines that bring data in from many sources and process it at scale. The third covers orchestration and the core data models that the rest of the Analytics Team builds on. The fourth covers the practices that keep the platform reliable, secure and affordable to run.
Data Platform and Infrastructure
Imagine’s analytics platform runs on AWS and ClickHouse Cloud, with infrastructure managed as code. In a small team, this role carries the infrastructure work that a larger organisation would split across dedicated platform or DevOps staff, limited to the scope of the analytics platform.
Build and maintain the platform’s AWS infrastructure, including storage, compute, networking, the data catalogue, secrets and access management (S3, EC2, Glue Data Catalog, Lake Formation, IAM, Secrets Manager).
Manage infrastructure as code in Terraform, keeping environments reproducible, version-controlled and reviewable.
Administer the ClickHouse Cloud warehouse, including service configuration, user and role management, and monitoring of performance and capacity.
Host and maintain the team’s self-hosted tools, including Apache Superset for BI and Apache Airflow for orchestration. This covers deployment, upgrades, authentication and availability. The Senior BI & Data Analyst manages the dashboards and content within Superset.

title: Senior Backend Engineer
description:
Senior Backend Engineer
About us
We're creating the foundational backend systems that power private market access, from secure authentication and transaction processing to portfolio management and regulatory compliance.
The Role
We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to own the systems where money moves and balances have to be correct — the ledger, transaction processing, and the settlement and reconciliation workflows behind our platform. This is the correctness core of what we build. If a balance is wrong, a transaction double-processes, or a reconciliation silently drifts, nothing else we build matters.
You'll design the double-entry ledger, the money-movement engine, and the long-running state machines that carry complex financial workflows to completion reliably over hours, days, or weeks. You'll reason about idempotency, concurrency, partial failure, and replay as a matter of habit, not as an afterthought.
You'll own core infrastructure decisions and set the standard for how we build financial systems.
Requirements
What You'll Do
Design and build the double-entry ledger and money-movement engine that all transactions reconcile against
Model complex financial workflows as robust, observable state machines that run reliably over long periods
Guarantee financial correctness under concurrency: idempotent operations, transactional integrity, and reconciliation that ties out to the cent
Handle partial-failure and replay cases so no event is lost, duplicated, or applied twice
Build secure, well-versioned APIs
Design and optimize PostgreSQL schemas and data models
Debug production issues and own the reliability of mission-critical financial workflows
What We're Looking For
5+ years of backend development on production systems
Demonstrated money-movement correctness experience: you've built a ledger, settlement system, payments core, or transaction-processing system and can talk in detail about how you kept it correct
Concurrency and idempotency depth: you can explain, from experience, how you handled double-processing, race conditions on balances, and replay
Reconciliation experience: you've built or owned systems that had to tie out exactly, and you know what happens when they don't
Strong TDD practices: you write tests first and maintain comprehensive coverage
Domain-Driven Design expertise: you model complex financial domains accurately
Deep PostgreSQL knowledge: schema design, transactions, isolation levels, optimization
Strong in a modern backend stack: we work in TypeScript/Node.js, Go and on the JVM ecosystem; we value real depth in either and the range to pick up the other
• Cloud deployment experience
Startup mentality: comfortable with ambiguity, high autonomy, driving solutions without detailed specs
Nice to Have
Payments, banking, brokerage, or investment-platform systems experience
Securities, custody, or portfolio/NAV domain knowledge
Event-driven architectures and message queues
Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, CloudFormation)
Understanding of KYC/AML or compliance frameworks
Accounting principles or financial modeling

title: Remote Senior Software Engineer, (OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor)
description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week
Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.
Check out this Loom video for more details:
We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense
Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer
This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing
Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code
What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:
Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
Would this interaction build or erode trust?
You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are
Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
High bar for what good engineering looks like
Nice to have
Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards
Engagement details
Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location
• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible
Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

title: Remote Python Senior Software Engineer, AI Training
description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week
Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.
Check out this Loom video for more details:
We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense
Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer
This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing
Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code
What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:
Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
Would this interaction build or erode trust?
You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are
Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
High bar for what good engineering looks like
Nice to have
Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards
Engagement details
Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location
• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible
Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

Role Summary
Mozayel LLC, a US-registered company, is seeking a remote React Native (Expo) Developer to join its development team. The developer will be responsible for developing, maintaining and improving cross-platform mobile applications, managing day-to-day development of the apps and its backend, and ensuring a reliable user experience across Android and iOS.
You will serve as the primary developer, taking ownership of development and the codebase, implementing new features, fixing issues, and maintaining overall application performance. You will work closely with a QA tester and the company founder to plan, develop, test, and deliver updates.
Compensation is paid monthly in USD and will be determined based on experience and technical qualifications. Candidates will be asked to complete a paid trial task before receiving a final offer.

Duties and Responsibilities
Design and develop new mobile applications from the ground up for Android and iOS.
Build, maintain, and improve cross-platform applications using modern mobile development technologies.
Develop new features, improve existing functionality, troubleshoot technical issues, and resolve bugs.
Design, develop, and maintain backend systems, databases, APIs, and server-side functionality.
Develop web-based applications and administrative platforms.
Take ownership of the complete software development lifecycle, from initial planning and architecture to development, testing, and deployment.
Write clean, maintainable, scalable, and well-structured code.
Implement secure authentication, data management, access controls, and reliable data synchronization.
Ensure applications support multiple languages, internationalization (i18n), and right-to-left (RTL) layouts where required.
Maintain application stability, performance, security, and compatibility across devices.
Identify technical improvements, investigate complex problems, and implement effective solutions.
Follow professional software development practices, including version control, code reviews, testing, and documentation.
Collaborate with team members to plan development priorities, evaluate progress, and deliver reliable software.
Stay current with modern development technologies, tools, and industry best practices.

Job Requirements
Minimum 3 years of professional mobile application development experience.
Proven experience developing and publishing at least one React Native / Expo application on both Google Play and the Apple App Store. Applicants must provide links to previously published applications.
Strong proficiency in TypeScript, JavaScript, React, and React Native.
Practical experience building and maintaining backend systems, relational databases, APIs, and server-side functionality.
Experience with database design, security policies, migrations, and serverless functions. Familiarity with Supabase or equivalent backend platforms is required.
Solid understanding of Git, version control, branching strategies, code reviews, and continuous integration.
Experience developing responsive user interfaces and maintaining consistent application behavior across different devices.
Practical experience with internationalization (i18n), multilingual applications, and right-to-left (RTL) layouts.
Understanding of application security, performance optimization, debugging, and error monitoring.
Ability to independently develop new applications and take responsibility for technical decisions.
Good written and verbal English communication skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with mobile application build automation, application store submissions, and over-the-air updates.
Experience with offline-first applications and reliable data synchronization.
Experience with server-side document and PDF generation.
Familiarity with application monitoring, crash reporting, and performance analysis tools.
Knowledge of Dari or Pashto is an advantage.
Experience using AI-assisted development tools effectively to improve development productivity.
Experience working independently in remote development environments.

Send your application to business@mozayel.com .
Use AFM-SD-001 as the exact email subject line.

Job Summary
We are seeking qualified, dedicated, and full-time English Language Teachers and Computer Trainers to join our academic team. English Language Teachers will deliver comprehensive English language courses, while Computer Trainers will provide practical instruction in computer programs and short courses such as CIT, DIT, MS Office, Windows, and other relevant applications. Candidates should demonstrate strong subject knowledge, effective teaching skills, professionalism, and a commitment to students’ academic and practical development.
Duties and Responsibilities
English Language Teacher

Prepare daily lesson plans and teaching materials for effective classroom instruction.

This team owns the capacity plan that keeps compute supply ahead of demand across every region we operate in — the forecasting, buffer policy, and provisioning systems that make sure a project never runs into a wall it didn't know was there.

Build and tune capacity alerting so headroom, quota, and reservation issues surface months out rather than at the moment of impact
Support the demand gate — helping intake large customer commitments, launches, migrations, and new regions so they reach the plan before they reach the fleet

title: Security Software Engineer
description:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.
The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.
Canonical is looking for exceptional security-focused software engineers to be integrated across product teams. While they also contribute to the product as engineers, their primary focus is to challenge the entire team to think more deeply about security through state-of-the-art practices such as threat modeling, table-top exercises, architecture and design reviews, static analysis tools, and fuzzing, among others.
These roles encompass all aspects of product security, including feature development, vulnerability response, proactive security, and open source community participation. Engineers in these roles collaborate closely with other Canonical teams, customers, and partners across the open source ecosystem.
Each product engineering team at Canonical reserves one or two openings for security-oriented software engineers. We also develop a number of products driven entirely by security needs, such as our AppArmor kernel investments and the Ubuntu Security Guide (USG). As the publisher of Ubuntu, we also handle long-term security response for the entire operating system and open source ecosystem. Working with tens of thousands of upstreams means that we need to be fluent in every major programming language and design, build, and adopt sophisticated tools that enable us to work at scale and speed with confidence.
Apply here if you are an exceptional security-focused software engineer, passionate about open source, and excited by Canonical's products and mission.
This role requires the ability to be productive in a globally distributed team through strong self-discipline and motivation. It also involves mandatory international travel at least twice a year, typically for one week.
Location: Worldwide, this is a globally remote role
What you'll do
Security roles might tackle any of the following:
Define, implement, and document new security features
Lead security-focused initiatives within a product engineering team
Analyze, fix, and test vulnerabilities in open source software
Contribute to Ubuntu and upstream open source projects to benefit the community
Audit and analyze source code for vulnerabilities
Integrate new tools into our security infrastructure, pipelines, and processes
Achieve and retain various security certifications
Extend and enhance Linux cryptographic components to meet country-specific compliance requirements, such as FIPS and Common Criteria (CC) certifications
Work with external partners to develop Center for Internet Security (CIS) benchmarks
Design and develop hardening automation for Ubuntu
Stay up to date with trends and developments in the security industry
Develop, test, and maintain new software capabilities
Provide guidance and support to other engineering teams on security best practices
What we are looking for in you
An exceptional academic track record from both high school and university
Undergraduate degree in Computer Science or STEM, or a compelling narrative about your alternative path
A track record of going above and beyond expectations
Thorough understanding of the common categories of security vulnerabilities and how to fix them
Knowledge of modern software engineering techniques
Familiarity with open source development tools and methodologies
